summary: Kickoff for a 4-week POC to validate latency, throughput and output fidelity for an inference-based claims assistant. Primary decisions: hosted API vs dedicated capacity vs private (VPC) and benchmark plan agreed (smoke tests then scaled runs).
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-06
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Klein (Redwood AE), Ravi Singh (Redwood SE), Sarah Moreno (CTO - Calyx), Liam O'Connor (Head of Platform), Priya Desai (SRE)

Summary (auto): discuss pilot success metrics, agree on benchmark plan and integration approach (SDK vs direct HTTP), document security requirements (SOC2, KMS, VPC peering), define next steps.

[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro — im jordan, account lead. ravi from the eng team will lead the bench and tech bits. can we do quick intros?
[00:18] Sarah: sure, sarah here, cto at calyx. we're looking to build a claims assistant to triage incoming claims, extract structured fields and suggested dispositions. primary concerns are latency during peak windows and PII handling.
[00:32] Liam: liam, head of platform. we'll own infra integration and security review. timeline is tight — insurance board wants a pilot that proves cost/benefit in about 4 weeks.
[00:45] Ravi: great, ravi. from redwood, i'll be the SE on the runbooks, benchmarks, etc. high level — we usually run a smoke benchmark then a scaled run, and test both OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDK flows to mirror your production traffic.
[01:02] Priya: priya — sres. curious about VPC/private deployment options. regulatory may ask for data residency.
[01:12] Jordan: noted. quick agenda: agree success criteria, workload shape, benchmark plan, what artifacts you can share, and security gating items.

[03:10] Liam: on success criteria — the board asked for p99 inference latency under 250ms for routing decisions and throughput of ~60 req/s during peak. cost target is under $X per 1M tokens, but that is flexible. more importantly fidelity of extracted fields (f1 > 0.88).
[03:40] Ravi: ok, so we should define two buckets: latency-sensitive routing calls (short context, <512 tokens) and heavy extraction with long context (2–3k tokens). batching and KV cache behave differently.
[04:05] Sarah: the heavy calls are about 15% of traffic but they blow up compute.

[06:22] Jordan: for POC we recommend a 3-stage benchmark: 1) smoke run (20–30 mins) using SDK with 1000 sample requests; 2) scaled run to simulate peak traffic for 3 hours; 3) fidelity run against a labelled sample for extraction metrics.
[06:45] Priya: how quickly can we run the scaled tests? we need to mirror authentication flows; we don't want to send real PII.
[06:58] Ravi: we can run with scrubbed anonymized payloads, plus a local token replay. we just need a sample file with request shapes and distribution (percent small vs large).

[09:10] Liam: on integration pattern: we currently use an in-house gateway that expects OpenAI-like endpoints. can we use Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoints as a drop-in?
[09:28] Ravi: yes, we support OpenAI-compatible endpoints and our SDKs. tradeoffs: direct HTTP OpenAI-compatible is easiest to drop-in; our SDKs give better observability (trace ids, batching hints) and streaming helpers.
[09:50] Jordan: plus the SDK will surface cost per route and token breakdown which is helpful for your finance folks.

[12:02] Sarah: function/tool calling — we need the assistant to call internal services: e.g., call a policy-lookup API, then return structured JSON with fields claim_type, estimated_payout, confidence. can redwood support function-calling patterns?
[12:22] Ravi: yes — our function-calling shim is compatible with the OpenAI function calling spec in most cases. caveat: if you want on-prem/private we need to validate network access and function invocation patterns. sometimes names and payloads get renamed in the transcription pipeline — small mismatch issues.
[12:50] Priya: we also require deterministic structured output for downstream systems. how do we ensure model outputs meet schema?
[13:04] Ravi: we recommend a two-step approach: 1) structured output constraints in prompt + schema enforcement in the SDK; 2) post-validate with your JSON schema and fall back to deterministic parsers. our console can run regression checks on a development prompt set.

[15:20] Jordan: security checklist — SOC2 reports, SAML SSO, RBAC, KMS/HSM integrations for key management, audit log access, and VPC peering/Private deployment options. which are must-haves for you?
[15:40] Liam: SOC2 and KMS are musts. SAML is required for our internal teams. VPC peering is requested if we move off hosted.
[15:55] Jordan: we have SOC2 docs and KMS integration patterns; i'll share the security pack after the call.

[18:30] Ravi: some technical notes: for long-context extraction we may recommend a quantized variant to reduce memory footprint, and tuning sequence length and kv cache. but quantization may affect f1 by a small delta. we should measure that in fidelity run.
[18:55] Sarah: acceptable if it stays within delta of 0.02 f1 ideally.

[21:05] Liam: what's the expected footprint to hit 60 req/s? do you have guidance on GPUs or instance counts?
[21:18] Ravi: rough ballpark: for a 50–100 token median reply on a 8k model, with continuous batching and two GPU workers you'd get ~40–70 rps depending on batching window. for peak headroom we'd suggest dedicated capacity with autoscale and burst. we'll size during the scaled bench.

[24:00] Jordan: timeline proposal: week 1 — align on success criteria and share artifacts; week 2 — smoke tests and SDK integration; week 3 — scaled benchmark and fidelity runs; week 4 — review and decision. that aligns with your 4-week ask.
[24:30] Sarah: that works. can we compress weeks 2 and 3 if we provide data early?
[24:45] Ravi: potentially yes, if we get sample traffic and credentials for smoke tests, we can run scaled tests in parallel in week 2.

[27:10] Priya: about observability — we need per-route latency breakdowns and token-level cost. does Redwood console show that?
[27:25] Jordan: yes, the console has per-model and per-route dashboards, trace ids, and token cost breakdown. we can give a short demo but it's not required for the POC.

[30:12] Liam: any blockers on our side to start? current blockers are legal review and anonymizing data.
[30:25] Jordan: for legal, i can loop in our legal contact and share standard pilot terms. for anonymization, a small script to hash or replace PHI works for the bench.

[33:45] Ravi: handshake on benchmarks: we'll provide a benchmark harness (python + artillery script) and instructions to replay requests over OpenAI-compatible endpoints and via SDK. we will capture p50/p90/p99 latency, throughput, tokens per request, and token cost.
[34:10] Sarah: for fidelity we will provide a labelled set (about 2k labelled samples) — is that enough?
[34:22] Ravi: yes 2k is good for a signal. we'll run extraction metrics and show F1, precision/recall.

[36:40] Liam: about function-calling security — can we restrict outbound calls from the model runtime so that only whitelisted internal endpoints are reachable?
[36:55] Ravi: yes for private deployments or dedicated pools with network policies we can restrict egress, and use a function-call proxy pattern for hosted. we'll document patterns.

[39:05] Jordan: recap and next steps — agreed success metrics: p99 < 250ms for routing; throughput 60 req/s peak; extraction F1 >= 0.88. deliverables: jordan sends pilot pricing and security pack; ravi shares benchmark harness and draft scripts; calyx provides anonymized sample traffic and labeled dataset.
[39:40] Sarah: confirmed. can we get a tentative date for the scaled run? week of 17th?
[39:50] Jordan: yes, week of 2026-02-17 — we'll propose a 3-hour window on Wed/Thu and confirm via calendar.

[41:10] Ravi: small note — for the SDK we can enable streaming + function call helpers which helps reduce latency for multi-turn flows. might be useful for your multi-step extraction.
[41:30] Priya: that sounds helpful. any impact on billing model?
[41:40] Jordan: billing is still token-based plus a small per-request egress for function calls in some tiers — i'll put the exact numbers in the pricing sheet.

[44:00] Liam: are there any known compatibility annoyances with our gateway when using OpenAI endpoints? some in-house gateways rewrite headers.
[44:12] Ravi: header rewriting can break streaming; we'll provide integration tips — including use of the SDK to avoid gateway rewrtes. also we sometimes see the model name mapping differences — e.g., "redwood/gpt-..." vs openai names — we'll document expected endpoint paths.

[45:30] Jordan: ok last thing, i'll include a short checklist in the follow-up: security docs, benchmark harness, sample payload format, and meeting times.
[45:48] Sarah: perfect thanks everyone.
[46:00] Jordan: thanks all, we'll follow up by Monday with materials.
[46:05] call end
